claims.claim: The six advertised block cardinalities sum to 76.
claims.evidence: Direct exact arithmetic gives 6+18+16+14+16+6=76. This verifies only the stated cardinality sum, not the existence of a corresponding algorithm.
claims.search_method: Direct arithmetic, independently reproduced by the exact-integer checker.

claims.claim: For any fixed allowed finite grid G and any three-Batdroid algorithm with a finite shade set Cl, the universe of configurations and its subset R_G reachable from Init(G) are finite.
claims.evidence: If G has N vertices and Cl has m shades, the source's collision-free configurations of exactly three Batdroids number at most binom(N,3)m^3: choose three distinct occupied vertices and one shade at each. N and m are finite, so the configuration universe and every subset of it, including R_G, are finite.
claims.search_method: Direct combinatorial proof from the source definition of configurations.

claims.claim: Fix an algorithm A, an allowed grid G, and a grid vertex u. Every execution from Init(G) satisfies the PEP recurrence condition for u if and only if the subgraph induced by reachable configurations in which u is unoccupied is acyclic; equivalently, every reachable directed walk of |R_G| edges contains a configuration occupying u.
claims.evidence: Let H_u be the reachable u-avoiding induced subgraph. A directed cycle in H_u can be preceded by its reachability path and repeated forever, producing a source execution eventually avoiding u. Conversely, a PEP-violating execution has an infinite tail in finite H_u, so some configuration repeats and yields a directed cycle. If a reachable walk of |R_G| edges avoided u throughout, its |R_G|+1 configurations would repeat, again yielding a cycle; conversely, a cycle can be repeated and truncated to such a walk.
claims.witness: Reachable avoiding cycle repeated indefinitely; alternatively, pigeonhole repetition among |R_G|+1 avoiding configurations.
claims.search_method: Direct finite-directed-graph proof checked against the source definitions of execution and PEP.

claims.claim: The acyclicity condition for a fixed G and u is equivalent to the existence of a bounded rank rho_u on reachable u-avoiding configurations that strictly decreases along every transition whose endpoints both avoid u.
claims.evidence: For a finite DAG, set rho_u(C) to the maximum length of a directed path beginning at C. It lies in {0,...,|R_G|-1}, and every internal edge C→C' gives rho_u(C)≥1+rho_u(C'). Conversely, a directed cycle would imply a strict inequality chain returning to its starting rank, which is impossible.
claims.witness: rho_u(C)=maximum length of a u-avoiding path starting at C.
claims.search_method: Direct construction and converse cycle argument.

claims.claim: The at-most-76-shade construction side of the target is exactly reduced to supplying a source-model tuple A=(Cl,Init,T) satisfying the target's ambiguity, legality, and reachable-state seriality requirements together with, for every allowed grid G and every u in G, a rank rho_u of the preceding kind on the full reachable configuration graph.
claims.evidence: Forward, any source-model solution has no reachable u-avoiding cycle for any G,u by claim 2, hence admits the ranks of claim 3. Reverse, if the complete legal and serial tuple and all ranks exist, a PEP-violating execution would have an infinite u-avoiding tail, contradicting strict descent on a finite ranked state set. The tuple qualifications retain exactly-three, visibility-one, no-common-chirality, ambiguity, and at-most-76-shade requirements; ranks are external proof certificates.
claims.search_method: Both implications proved directly using claims 2 and 3 and the authorized source model.

claims.claim: Given the source's 77-shade upper bound, the optimality side of the target is dually reduced to proving that every source-model-valid visibility-one three-Batdroid candidate with at most 76 shades, serial on its reachable configurations, has some allowed grid G and vertex u whose reachable u-avoiding configuration subgraph contains a directed cycle.
claims.evidence: The stated universal cycle result would exclude every at-most-76 candidate by producing a repeatable execution eventually avoiding u; the source's 77-shade construction would then make 77 optimal. Conversely, if 77 is optimal, every valid serial at-most-76 candidate fails PEP on some allowed grid and execution. Negating the source's PEP quantifiers supplies a vertex u eventually omitted by that execution, and finiteness then supplies the required reachable cycle.
claims.search_method: Direct quantifier negation followed by the finite-state cycle criterion.

claims.claim: For every signed orthogonal frame, whenever all nodes displayed by a selected one of the two advertised knight encounter branches lie in the finite grid, that selected branch is collision-free and swap-free and ends in K(q+r;a,r,f).
claims.evidence: After translating q to 0, the near branch has labeled states (r,2r,2r+f)→(r,2r+f,r+f)→(r+a,3r+f,r). The far branch has (r,2r,2r+f)→(r,2r+f,3r+f)→(r,r+f,3r+f)→(r+a,r,3r+f). Every displacement is idle or a signed unit; orthogonality keeps all simultaneous positions distinct, and no pair reverses the same edge. Both endpoint sets are {r,r+a,3r+f}=K(r;a,r,f). Exhaustive enumeration checked both branches for all 48 frames.
claims.witness: 96 branch/frame cases, all passing unit-move, collision, swap, and endpoint assertions.
claims.search_method: Independent exhaustive enumeration using integer triples.

claims.claim: The finite-grid node-existence hypothesis in the revised knight-encounter claim is necessary in the source model.
claims.evidence: In the allowed grid {0,1,2,3}^3, q=(1,0,0), a=(0,0,1), r=(1,0,0), f=(0,1,0) give valid staging vertices (2,0,0),(3,0,0),(3,1,0), while q+3r+f=(4,1,0) is outside the grid. Both branches use that later vertex, so staging-node existence alone cannot make either branch a source-grid trace.

claims.claim: At the advertised ordinary-transition staging configuration, whenever all nodes displayed by a selected choice lie in the finite grid, that choice is collision-free and swap-free and yields the stated diagonal frame.
claims.evidence: Translate q to 0. For the e-choice, (0,d,f)→(0,d,e+f), ending at D(0;d,e,f). For the d-choice, (0,d,f)→(0,d,d+f)→(e,0,d+f), ending at D(0;e,d,f). Since d,e,f are signed units on distinct axes, all moves are unit or idle, every simultaneous position triple is distinct, and no edge is traversed in opposite directions. All 48 frames, two d/e orderings, and two choices were enumerated.
claims.search_method: Independent exhaustive enumeration using integer triples.

claims.claim: The finite-grid node-existence hypothesis in the revised ordinary-transition claim is necessary in the source model.
claims.evidence: In {0,1,2,3}^3, q=(0,0,0), d=a=(1,0,0), r=(0,1,0), f=(0,0,1), e=-r give valid staging nodes q,q+d,q+f. The e-choice requires q+e+f=(0,-1,1), which is not a grid vertex. Thus the unqualified selected choice is not a source-model move.

claims.claim: From the advertised outer-reset staging configuration, whenever all nodes displayed by a selected edge choice, short-axis choice, and conversion sign lie in the finite grid, that selected trace is collision-free and swap-free and ends in K(s;y,d,x).
claims.evidence: Translate q to 0, so s=d. The train shifts (0,d,2d)→(d,2d,2d+x). For sign +, subsequent labeled states are (d,2d+x,3d+x)→(d,d+x,3d+x); for sign − they are (d,2d+x,d+x)→(d,3d+x,d+x). The handoff moves d to d+y and the occupant of d+x to d, giving endpoint set {d,d+y,3d+x}=K(s;y,d,x). Because d,x,y are independent signed units, all moves, collisions, and swaps check exactly. Enumeration covered 48×2×2×2=384 cases.
claims.search_method: Independent exhaustive enumeration using integer triples.

claims.claim: The finite-grid node-existence hypothesis in the revised outer-reset claim is necessary in the source model.
claims.evidence: In {0,1,2,3}^3, take q=(1,1,1), d=a=(1,0,0), r=(0,1,0), f=(0,0,1), e=-r, x=-f, y=e, and s=q+d. The staging and shifted nodes all lie in the grid, but the +d conversion requires s+2d+x=(4,1,0), outside it. Hence the displayed-node condition cannot be omitted.

claims.claim: The reset recurrence h=-f, {d,e}={a,-r}, {x,y}={h,e}, (a,r,f)->(y,d,x) is closed on the 48 signed orthogonal frames for all four choices.
claims.evidence: For any input frame, d,e,h=-f remain signed unit vectors on the three distinct coordinate axes. Since x,y reorder h,e, the successor (y,d,x) also uses each axis exactly once. Independent enumeration checked all four successors of all 48 frames, totaling 192 closed edges.
claims.witness: Every one of 192 recurrence edges had its endpoint in the enumerated 48-frame set.
claims.search_method: Algebraic closure proof plus exhaustive exact enumeration.

claims.claim: For the abstract reset recurrence, two signed orthogonal frames are mutually reachable if and only if their coordinate-sign products agree; consequently the 48-frame digraph has exactly two strongly connected components of size 24, each of directed diameter 3.
claims.evidence: The four successors are (-r,a,-f), (-f,a,-r), (a,-r,-f), and (-f,-r,a). Each permutes axes and flips two vector signs, so the sign product is invariant. Breadth-first search from every one of the 48 frames reached exactly the 24 frames with the same product. Every start had distance layers 1,4,13,6 at distances 0,1,2,3, proving strong connectivity within each invariant class and directed diameter exactly 3.
claims.witness: Two 24-state reachability classes; 1,152 same-sign ordered pairs reachable; maximum shortest-path distance 3.
claims.search_method: Independent exhaustive construction of all 192 edges and BFS from every frame.

claims.claim: The abstract reset recurrence admits a two-cycle under one repeated allowed choice, so closure and existential frame reachability alone cannot imply frame-wide visitation for every choice sequence.
claims.evidence: Repeatedly choosing d=-r, e=a, x=-f, y=a sends (a,r,f) to (a,-r,-f), then back to (a,r,f). The intermediate frame is distinct because r and f are nonzero. The checker verified this same repeated-choice two-cycle from all 48 starting frames, which directly disproves any universal frame-visitation inference from closure and existential reachability alone.
claims.search_method: Symbolic substitution plus exhaustive exact verification over all frames.

claims.claim: The exact target remains unresolved by this draft.
claims.evidence: The draft supplies no explicit at-most-76 shade set, Init mapping, or total local-view transition function, and no proof of universal PEP for such a tuple. It also supplies no theorem excluding every at-most-76 candidate. Its graph reductions and conditional coordinate lemmas therefore establish neither alternative in the source target.
claims.search_method: Compared every substantive construction and lower-bound obligation in the authorized source target against the complete authorized draft.

target_evidence: The draft correctly does not claim a complete solution. Its finite-state cycle/rank equivalences and independently verified conditional trace and frame-recurrence results are correct, nonvacuous partial lemmas. However, it gives neither a source-model algorithm with at most 76 shades nor a lower bound excluding all such algorithms, so the exact target remains open. The parent's PARTIAL resolution label is accurate.
checks_performed: Read only /evidence/source.json and /evidence/parent.json; used no web or other evidence, arm, receipt, retrieval, prompt, or prior-run material.
Checked the source definitions of finite grids, configurations, one-round reachability, executions, ambiguity, and PEP.
Reproved the finite-state cycle, bounded-walk, rank, construction, and lower-bound equivalences with their quantifiers.

The checker verified the shade sum; 96 knight cases; 192 ordinary-transition cases; 384 outer-reset cases; all three boundary witnesses; all 192 recurrence edges; two 24-state SCCs of directed diameter 3; and 48 repeated-choice two-cycles.
